design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (maturity_due_and_payable_cases, env_0064). Frozen 2026-10-21 10:40:00 EDT (Wednesday).

1. DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 4, 4]}. Assignment: root maturity_ext_first_extension_sizing = 6 factors; maturity_ext_successor_runway = 5; maturity_ext_successor_response_window = 4; maturity_ext_successor_evidence_window = 4. Tree: 3 prerequisite problems, 3 value_input edges (floor max(3-1,1)=2) + 1 state_gate edge. Task 1 draw (for headroom): prerequisite 1, factors [6, 6].

2. WHY A GOOD TEST. Claire Pendleton, executor of Harriet Pendleton's estate, asks only for "the extra time" her mother requested so the house sale is not cut off. Nothing she says names the work. To book that extension correctly the agent must discover from the charter that (a) Harriet's documented death has not yet superseded the Property Charge Default event on the case and the reclassification carries the resolution deadline forward by a successor runway, (b) the successor is owed her own due-and-payable notice and options letter, which set a successor response deadline, (c) the extension on a deceased borrower's case waits on an intent declared by the successor herself, which only Claire can file (customer's own write), and only then (d) size the extension. Every write carries a number computed from records spread over five products (maturity case/requests/events, residency death notices and inspections, Summit loan balance, property-charge arrangement ledger, Summit reserve status). Difficulty comes from reading prerequisite sentences, reconciling records and arithmetic — never from tool choice (each problem has exactly one tool).

3. SCOPE / OCCUPATION. Task 0 claims maturity_ext_successor_runway (reclassify_case_to_death_eeacbce3, agent), maturity_ext_successor_response_window (mail_successor_due_notices_bb6e23d7, agent), maturity_ext_successor_evidence_window (declare_successor_intent_94ee6efc, user), maturity_ext_first_extension_sizing (grant_first_extension_77f15011, agent). Reserved for task 1 (independent space): the further extension on a Summit case and the customer's own further-extension request (maturity_ext_further_extension_ask -> submit_further_extension_request_d5cdfbad, user; maturity_ext_further_extension_sizing -> grant_further_extension_50c8b1d2, agent), on a living-borrower Summit case whose closing is evidenced by a payoff statement. No policy or tool overlaps.

4. ROUTE-AROUND DECISIONS (frozen base, recorded honestly). (i) maturity_called_due triggers hecm/jumbo due_and_payable for every loan program, so no task tool may write it; call-due states are seeded. (ii) HECM periods are HUD-fixed, so all factor ladders live on Summit (Cedarline's own proprietary schedules). (iii) The customer's own figure (evidence_due_days) has no field: it is printed on the declaration receipt and is part of the declaration's reference number; the docstring says exactly that. (iv) Owed notices are folded into the write that owes them (successor notice pair; extension letter with the grant). (v) Declared overwrites retire base gates whose evidence cannot exist for these acts and restate their in-force content: notice once-per-date (pair), the two intent-recording gates (filed and recorded in one act; same successor and response-window tests, deadline day counting), HUD approval and extension count for Summit extensions, and (round 2) the inherited 'when the appraisal is older than appraisal_valid_months, a new appraisal is ordered' for Summit extensions: no order at the grant, the appraisal is replaced by a new one when a payoff or sale is next evaluated; every other extension still orders it wherever the plan's reappraisal-for-extension setting calls for one. Each replaced_by names its scope and both sibling extension scopes.
5. FACTOR CARDS (tier taken / evidence rows / baseline figure; recomputed by check_compute).
 maturity_ext_successor_runway = 33 (baseline 19):
  household_runway (parameter, residency): latest finding 2026-08-21 occupied_by_others (Claire staying while Harriet was in hospital/rehab; near-miss: 2025-08-19 occupied_by_borrower is older) -> 60 | baseline 30 -> 3.
  report_anchor (method, multi-source): phone report 2026-10-07 AND accepted mailed notice 2026-10-13 (6 days) -> start on the phone date, offset -17 | baseline notice date (offset -11) -> 39.
  equity_runway (parameter): 688,412.37 / 1,265,000.00 = 54.42 -> +7 | 26.
  charge_runway (parameter, multi-source, setaside): advances 10,596.22 > 2,000.00 AND reserve depleted -> -10 | 43.
  underway_runway (parameter, multi-source): received listing request AND most recent accepted declaration (Harriet's) declares a sale -> -7 | 40.
  result MX(0, -17+60+7-10-7) = 33 -> deadline 2026-10-24 -> 2026-11-26.
 maturity_ext_successor_response_window = 29 (baseline 30):
  sale_underway_window (parameter): request + sale declaration -> 21 | 42.
  appraisal_age_window (parameter): appraisal 2026-04-28 is 5 whole months old at 2026-10-21 (near-miss: October minus April = 6 is the stale tier) -> +5 | 22.
  charge_window (parameter, setaside): -5 | 36.
  counting_convention (method, residency; round 2: keyed to the occupancy finding, not the notice channel): occupied_by_others -> 21 business days from Wed 2026-10-21 = Thu 2026-11-19 = 29 | plain calendar -> 21.
 maturity_ext_successor_evidence_window = 14 (baseline 59):
  on_file_evidence_window (parameter): request + sale declaration -> 14 | 30.
  evidence_clock_anchor (method; round 2 tiers): not in extension period AND resolution deadline 2026-11-26 only 7 days after response deadline 2026-11-19 -> clock starts on the declaration date, offset 0 | baseline response deadline (offset 29) -> 43.
  appraisal_evidence_allowance (parameter): 5 whole months -> +7 (near-miss as above: careless 6 -> +14) | 7.
  charge_evidence_cut (parameter, setaside): -7 | 21.
  result MX(1, 0+14+7-7) = 14 -> evidence due 2026-11-04.
 maturity_ext_first_extension_sizing = 40 (baseline 34):
  document_horizon (method; round 3 tiers): listing dated 2026-07-03, 91 days before the 2026-10-02 receipt (more than 90: aged listing) -> to 150 days after the listing date, 2026-11-30, minus 2026-11-26 = 4 | baseline 180 days after the document date (2026-12-30: 34) -> 70. Near-miss: 90-or-fewer days would be the fresh tier (+180).
  occupant_allowance (parameter, residency): +15 | 30 (floor).
  equity_cushion (parameter): +7 | 33.
  advance_exposure_cut (parameter, multi-source, setaside): -10 | 50.
  carried_request (parameter, multi-source, residency): filed by Harriet 2026-10-02, died 2026-10-06 after receipt -> +10 | 30 (floor).
  successor_takeover (parameter): most recent accepted declaration is Claire's of 2026-10-21, 0 days before the grant -> +14 | 30 (floor).
  result MN(90, MX(30, 4+15+7+10+14-10)) = 40 (guard: 1 request awaiting a decision) -> 2027-01-05.
6. FACTOR INDEPENDENCE TABLE (no factor reads another factor's binding; plain bindings deadline_now, borrower_id, mailing_date, declaration_date, response_deadline_now/resolution_deadline_now (E, owned by the anchor), window_count, pending_requests are reads/assembly/guards outside factors). Runway: household<-residency_events; report_anchor<-residency_submissions + deadline_now; equity<-jumbo balance + appraisal; charge<-propcharge ledger + setaside; underway<-maturity_requests (requests, accepted declarations). Window: sale_underway<-requests + declarations; appraisal_age<-appraisal_date; charge<-ledger + reserve; counting_convention<-residency_events + weekday (transforms window_count; its tiers read only the finding). Evidence: on_file<-requests + declarations; anchor<-status + response/resolution deadlines + latest grant; appraisal<-appraisal_date; charge<-ledger + reserve. Extension: horizon<-pending request document/date/receipt + deadline_now; occupant<-residency_events; equity<-balance + appraisal; exposure<-ledger + reserve; carried<-request filer/receipt + death date + borrower_id; takeover<-latest accepted declaration date.
7. METHOD TIERS PAIRWISE (one distinguishing input per pair). report_anchor: phone-start vs death+30 (a phone report exists vs not); phone-start vs notice date (written notice within 10 days of the phone report vs later); death+30 vs notice date (notice more than 30 days after death vs not). counting_convention: business days vs weekend-roll (finding occupied_by_others vs vacant); business vs plain (occupied_by_others vs any other/no finding); weekend-roll vs plain (vacant vs other; differs whenever the calendar end is a Saturday or Sunday). evidence_clock_anchor: grant date vs declaration date (status extension_period vs due_and_payable); grant date vs response deadline (same input); declaration date vs response deadline (resolution deadline no more than 30 days after the response deadline vs more). document_horizon (round 3): commitment+60 vs listing+150 (document type); listing+150 vs listing+180 (listing dated more than 90 vs no more than 90 days before receipt); commitment+60 vs listing+180 (document type). Monotone: an older listing never earns more than a fresher one (at the 90-day boundary the end drops from receipt+90 to receipt+59).
8. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Step 13 reclassify: maturity_agg_multi_holding (no gate on reclassified; scope: open case + higher-ranked documented event; case status due_and_payable, accepted death notice rs_mail). Step 15 notices: maturity_notices (gate retired by declared overwrite; once-per-date restated for the pair; no notice ever to Claire). Step 17 declaration: maturity_intent_appraisal (gates retired by overwrite, restated: declarant profile_type successor_in_interest linked to Harriet; filed 2026-10-21 <= response deadline 2026-11-19 written in step 15; base rule: deadline day still counts). Step 19 extension: maturity_extensions extension_request_on_file (rq_ext1 received, listing_agreement in plan's extension_evidence) and extension_before_deadline (time; anchor maturity_cases.resolution_deadline, relation not_after, inclusive, grace 0: request 2026-10-02 vs deadline 2026-10-24 in force at receipt; a 2026-10-25 receipt would be declined, a 2026-10-24 receipt processed); HUD gate and count gate retired by overwrite and restated (Summit: Cedarline approves; extensions granted 0 -> number 1; max 2 under the death plan).

9. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: maturity case f0fbf2ac on Summit loan 7412058836 (Harriet's single open case). Extension request: the only extension_request rq_ext1 (received). Declarations: rq_intent (Harriet, 2026-05-11, accepted) — the most recent accepted declaration until Claire declares. Death notices: rs_phone (rejected) gives only the telephone report date; rs_mail (accepted) the documentation; Claire's letters testamentary (supporting_document, accepted 2026-10-13) confirm her successor capacity; her profile opened 2026-10-07 with her first call (round 2: no longer predates the death). Ledger: two propcharge advances, no repayment; reserve depleted. Jumbo/setaside ledgers not seeded (no read needs them; closure gate).
10. ROW ROLES (delete -> change). rs_phone: anchor becomes notice date (33->39). re_res26: runway 30 (->3), business-day convention lost (29->21), occupant 0. jumbo balance: equity tiers. pc_adv1/2 + reserve status: charge tiers. rq_ext1: underway/sale/on-file tiers, horizon, carried request, the request granted. rq_intent: sale-declaration tiers of R/W/E. Appraisal 2026-04-28: appraisal tiers (whole-month near-miss). Letters: successor confirmation evidence for the declaration. Customers: Claire (caller, successor, recipient, declarant) and Harriet (borrower of record).
11. PERSONA DESIGN. Brisk, tired executor; volunteers only the goal and opening facts true in initial_state (death, listing since summer, request sent early October, letters saying resolved by October 24 = resolution_deadline 2026-10-24). Identity (name, 4155546620, 1966-09-22) on request; loan number, death date, phone-then-mail reporting, listing details, her stay in the house since August while her mother was in hospital and rehab (round 2: consistent with the 2026-08-21 occupied_by_others finding), unpaid advances only when asked. Intent line verbatim "we are selling the house; the loan gets paid out of the sale". Never mentions reclassification, notices, response windows or her own declaration; runs the handed-over tool with the agent's figures; stops on the new deadline. No extra asks.
12. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Edges (policy_source verbatim in each blocked rule): window <- runway (state_gate; "...not mailed, and the successor response window is not counted, until the case's event type is the death of the last surviving borrower."; false: variant Property Charge Default); evidence <- window (value_input on clock_start_offset; "...taken only after the case shows a response deadline that falls on or after the day of the declaration." — round 2: aligned with the deadline-day-counts acceptance rule; false: response_deadline 2026-05-24); extension <- evidence (value_input on takeover_allowance; "...granted only after the case records the resolution intent declared by a successor in interest of that borrower."; false: successor_customer_id = Harriet, latest declaration 2026-05-11); extension <- runway (value_input on horizon_days; "...is not sized until the case's event type reads the death of the last surviving borrower."; false: variant charge default, deadline 2026-10-24). Directions mixed. State-form uniqueness: only reclassify sets variant_name; only the notice tool sets response_deadline; only the declaration tool records a successor's declaration. Order R, W, E, F1 unique. Deletion runs: skip notices -> evidence 1 (vs 14); skip declaration -> extension 26 raised to the 30-day floor = 30 (vs 40); skip reclassification -> extension: horizon from 2026-10-24 to 2026-11-30 = 37, then 37 + 15 + 7 + 10 + 14 - 10 = 73 (vs 40); notices 29 (state gate). Tools validate nothing (only a missing-case Error).
13. STANDARD SOLUTION (20 actions). find_customers(full_name) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> find_maturity_cases(Harriet) -> find_maturity_requests -> find_maturity_case_events -> find_residency_profiles -> find_residency_submissions -> find_residency_events -> find_jumbo_loans -> find_propcharge_plans -> find_propcharge_transactions -> find_setaside_accounts -> unlock/call reclassify(event_date 2026-10-06, 33) -> unlock/call notices(Claire, 29) -> unlock_user/call_user declaration(Claire, sell_property, 14) -> unlock/call extension(rq_ext1, Claire, number 1, 40). The appraisal (5 months) is not older than the plan's validity, so no reappraisal question arises.
14. VERIFICATION (repo root, round 2 full block): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK; SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK; GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK; TRACEABILITY misses only unlock tool names (docs unpublished). Recompute 33 / 29 / 14 / 40 equals gold (round 3).
15. EDGE PROBES (scratch copies; results unchanged 33/29/14/40 after round 3). Round 1: a paid-off second Summit loan with an active reserve on it (reads filtered by the case's jumbo_loan_id), a later declined financing-commitment request, a later rejected portal death notice, a later declined retain declaration by Claire, an inspection order without outcome. Round 2 (changed reads): a declined retain declaration dated 2026-10-20 (takeover/declaration reads use accepted only), a declined commitment request dated 2026-10-05 (horizon/listing-age reads use received only), a rejected supporting document. Absent records: no appraisal -> equity share 100 / 'missing' tiers; no inspection -> standard runway, plain calendar count, no allowance; no reserve -> not active; no arrangement -> 0 advances; no request awaiting a decision -> extension guard 0; no response deadline -> clock starts on the declaration date (stated tier); extension period with no grant on record -> response deadline (stated); no accepted declaration -> takeover allowance 0 (stated, no sentinel). Date edges: response deadline equal to the declaration date is taken (deadline day counts) and lands on tier 2 or 3 with offset 0; extensions floored at 30 days (round 2: no zero-day extension); listing exactly 90 days before receipt stays on the fresh-listing tier (round 3).
16. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Reading only the rules, docstrings, persona and lookup returns gives the same four writes, order and figures above; the only judgement points (which request, which declaration, which death notice, which inspection) are each pinned by a stated selection rule (most recent received / accepted / latest finding, with a stated same-day tie rule).
17. REACHABLE-DOMAIN TABLE (round 2, CG-3 class; every tier reachable and non-universal within its policy's scope incl. prerequisite sentences). R (death supersedes on an open Summit case): household 60/20/30 (finding others/vacant/other-none); report_anchor (phone<=10d / no phone & notice >30d after death / else); equity 15/7/0; charge 10/5/0 (unrepaid >2000 & reserve not active / 0<x<=2000 & not active / none or active); underway 7/3/0 (supported request & sale-retain declaration / declaration without request / no such declaration) — all reachable. W (successor package on a death-reclassified Summit case): sale_underway 21/25/30; appraisal 15/10/5/0 (none possible within 30 days of the call); charge 5/2/0; counting (others/vacant/other) — all reachable (round 2: the channel-keyed fall-through that needed an accepted phone notice is gone). E (successor declaring with a response deadline on or after the declaration day): on_file 14/21/30 (a death case may carry no sale declaration yet); anchor (extension_period with a grant / not and resolution <= 30 days after response / not and > 30) — all reachable; appraisal 21/14/7/0; charge 7/3/0. F1 (first extension, Summit death case, successor declaration recorded, request listing or commitment): horizon (commitment / listing more than 90 days old at receipt / listing no more than 90 days old; a listing past its 180-day term shows no active marketing and is declined by the inherited grant condition, so no tier relies on it); occupant 15/7/0; equity; exposure; carried (borrower-filed & died after receipt / filed by someone else / borrower-filed & received on or after death — the 'death case' part removed); takeover (declared <= 7d / 8-30d / > 30d before the grant) — all reachable. A (re-filing a pending further request): span (terms issued / contract only / neither); funds 21/7/0; occupant; appraisal; filing lead 5/2/0 (the universal 'awaiting a decision' part removed; guard stated as a separate zero rule); reserve 7/14/0 — all reachable. F2 (further extension on a current listing or commitment request): measure (commitment with payoff statement / commitment without / listing); equity; prior grant (listing granted > 60d ago / listing <= 60d / commitment); sale price review (contract below 95 / 95-100 / 100 or more or no contract; round 3, replaces payoff readiness, which double-counted the payoff statement already used by the measure); occupant; reappraisal — all reachable. Method floors kept: R, W, E, F1, A, F2 each keep exactly one method factor; factor counts unchanged (5,4,4,6,6,6).
18. REVISION LOG (round 2, audit policy_task r1). CG-1: E's prerequisite sentence said 'falls after the day of the declaration' while its acceptance rule counts the deadline day -> sentence now 'falls on or after'; tiers re-derived. CG-2: E edge condition used 'the frozen date' -> now 'on or after the day the successor declares' (copied into prerequisite_closure). CG-3a: E anchor tiers rebuilt (extension period / short runway / response deadline baseline) -> E result 43 -> 14, all proof text swept. CG-3b/c/d: F1 horizon tiers keyed to listing age; estate_resolution replaced by successor_takeover (recency); carried_request tier 2 'death case' part dropped; values unchanged (87). CG-3 W observation: counting convention re-keyed to the occupancy finding (value unchanged 29). T0-F1: appraisal moved to 2026-04-28 to give E (and W) a whole-month near-miss. T0-C1: F1<-R skip arithmetic corrected to 120. Observations: Claire's profile now opened 2026-10-07 with letters testamentary seeded; persona places Harriet in hospital/rehab during the 2026-08-21 inspection; zero-day extensions replaced by a 30-day floor.
19. REVISION LOG (round 3, audit r2). R2-N1: F1 document_horizon rebuilt — baseline is now 180 days after the supporting document's date (floor 30, cap plan days); tiers commitment+60 / aged listing (more than 90 days old at receipt) +150 / fresh listing +180; every tier reachable and monotone. Seed: rq_ext1 listing date 2026-07-03 (91 days), persona line 'signed July 3'. F1 gold 87 -> 40 (deadline 2027-01-05); closure, traces, tracing and this dossier swept. R2-N2 (task 1 policy) fixed charter-wide. Sibling-scenario lines applied to all six policies: every overwrite's replaced_by now restates the in-force base content first and then names its own scope (no 'sized by its own rule' phrasing); the window-count assembly sentence is generic ('base count with every addition made and every deduction taken'); assembly lives only in plain bindings/result. Probes re-run on changed reads (declined listing request with a later date, declined retain declaration): 33/29/14/40 unchanged; skip runs F1 73 (no R) and 30 (no E).

19. REVISION LOG (round 5, render_source r1 + XF recipe). Charter only; every task-0 figure unchanged (R 33, W 29, E 14, F1 40; baselines and factor sensitivities unchanged, COMPUTE match). A: each baseline now defines the quantity its factors act on and states the combination once with its order — R: base runway length (household_runway) -> runway length with every addition and deduction -> runway end date -> runway days, zero floor on the days; W: base count -> window count with additions/deductions made before the counting convention turns it into calendar days; E: base evidence window -> evidence window, clock start plus window, raised to 1 last; F1: measured extension -> extension length, raised to 30 then limited to the plan days after every addition and deduction. Factor sentences name the quantity they act on ('added to the extension length', 'taken off the runway length'). B: R's replaced_by restates the higher-rank reclassification trigger, new type and event date, new parameters governing and cure removal for every case; W's notices replaced_by restates the options-letter contents (intent options and response window) and the call-due replaced_by restates the successor-response-days deadline; E's replaced_by keeps 'for a deceased borrower's loan' and the plan's successor confirmation requirement; the reappraisal replaced_by no longer defers to a base rule. C: E clock — no response deadline -> declaration date, extension period with no grant on record -> response deadline, resolution deadline before the response deadline -> declaration date, all stated; appraisal ages no longer use a -1 sentinel (missing -> missing tier, dated after the event -> under 4 months); F1 — no accepted declaration -> nothing added (999 sentinel removed); another kind of document or an undated one -> evidence insufficient, first extension days zero; no date of death -> nothing added. Probes re-run on this world: removing Claire's declaration -> F1 takeover 0; undated document -> 0; R/W/E unchanged under the decoys listed above.

20. REVISION LOG (round 6, audit policy_task r5, R5-N1). Every 'most recent' pick now carries a stated tie rule and the compute implements it with a two-step pick (latest date, then latest recorded time on that date): R, W and E — accepted intent declarations made on one day: the one recorded later; R and F1 — accepted death notices received on one day: the one recorded later; F1 — extension requests received on one day: the one recorded later (request document, its date and its filer); R, W and F1 — inspection findings on one date: occupied by someone other than a borrower prevails over vacant, vacant over any other finding (residency events carry no recorded time). The two tools that write requests now stamp created_at in the records' own YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS form (_CalendarDays.record_time), so a request filed today orders correctly against seeded same-day rows. No tie exists in this world; figures unchanged (33/29/14/40). Same-day decoy probes: a later-recorded other-intent declaration moves R 33->40, W 29->42, E 14->30 (an earlier-recorded one leaves gold); a later-recorded same-day accepted death notice dated 2026-09-30 moves F1 40->30 (earlier-recorded leaves 40); a same-day occupied finding beside a vacant latest keeps the occupied tier in R, W and F1.
user_scenario:
You are Claire Pendleton, 60, calling Cedarline Reverse Mortgage from Charlotte. Your mother, Harriet Pendleton, died on October 6, 2026, and you are the executor of her estate. You are organized but worn out, you keep a folder of papers on the kitchen table, and you speak plainly and a little briskly; you apologize once for sounding tired. You open by saying your mother had a Summit reverse mortgage with Cedarline on her house at 2214 Hopedale Avenue, that the house has been listed for sale since the summer, and that your mother sent Cedarline a request for more time in early October, a few days before she passed. The letters she got said the loan had to be resolved by October 24, and you are calling because you want that extra time put in place so the sale is not cut off; you want Cedarline to take care of whatever is needed on its side, and you will handle personally anything that has to be done in your own name.

When the agent asks who you are, give your full name, Claire Pendleton; when asked for details to verify you, give your phone number 4155546620 and your date of birth, 1966-09-22 (September 22, 1966). Give your email, claire.pendleton@gmail.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 4471, only if the agent asks for something more. Your mother's loan number, 7412058836, and her date of death, 2026-10-06, you give only when asked. If the agent asks how Cedarline learned of the death, say you phoned on October 7 and then mailed in the death certificate, which they told you arrived October 13. If asked where the house stands, say it is still listed with the same listing agreement your mother sent in, MLS 4188201, signed July 3, and there is no offer yet. If asked whether anyone lives there, say you have been staying in the house since August, while your mother was in the hospital and then a rehabilitation center, and you are still there. If asked about the property taxes and insurance Cedarline paid earlier this year, say you know about them and they have not been paid back yet. If the agent asks what the estate intends to do with the house, say: we are selling the house; the loan gets paid out of the sale. You do not want to keep the house and you do not want to sign it over to Cedarline.

You do not know Cedarline's internal steps, and you do not suggest any. If the agent explains that something has to be done in your own name and hands it to you to complete, you do it right away using exactly the reference numbers, choice and figure the agent tells you, and you read back what your confirmation shows. You never supply numbers of your own for it. If the agent tells you about letters being mailed to you, you simply say that is fine and give no other address than the one on file.

Once the agent tells you the extension is granted and gives you the new resolution deadline, you repeat the new date back, thank the agent, and end the call. If the agent tells you the extension cannot be granted today, you ask once what you should do next, accept the answer, and end the call.

request_binding.action_semantics: A documented death of the last surviving borrower on a loan whose case is open owes a reclassification of that case (the death ranks first in supersede priority); no other write changes a case's event type, and nothing about it depends on what the caller asks.

edges.condition: The Summit case's variant_name reads Death of Last Surviving Borrower, the case having been reclassified from the event it was opened for after the borrower's documented death.
edges.policy_source: The successor's due-and-payable notice and options letter are not mailed, and the successor response window is not counted, until the case's event type is the death of the last surviving borrower.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen time the Summit case is still typed as the Property Charge Default it was opened for; Harriet's death (documented 2026-10-13) has not been applied to it, so the successor's notices and window are not yet due.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The reclassification writes variant_name = Death of Last Surviving Borrower (and event_date 2026-10-06) on the case.

edges.condition: The case's response_deadline falls on or after the day the successor declares, having been reset from the mailing of the successor's due-and-payable notice and options letter.
edges.policy_source: A successor's intent declaration, and the evidence due date it carries, are taken only after the case shows a response deadline that falls on or after the day of the declaration.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only response deadline on the case is the borrower's 2026-05-24, months before the 2026-10-21 declaration, so no response deadline on or after the day of the declaration is on the case.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Mailing Claire's due-and-payable notice and options letter sets response_deadline = 2026-11-19; with the resolution deadline 2026-11-26 only 7 days later, the evidence clock starts on the declaration date (offset 0) and the evidence due days are 14, instead of the 1 the lapsed 2026-05-24 deadline would give.

edges.condition: The case's successor_customer_id names a successor in interest linked to the deceased borrower and its successor_intent is retain_property or sell_property, recorded from that successor's own declaration.
edges.policy_source: A first extension on a deceased borrower's case is granted only after the case records the resolution intent declared by a successor in interest of that borrower.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only intent declaration on the case is Harriet's own (2026-05-11); the case records her as the person acting on it, so no intent declared by a successor in interest is recorded, and the most recent accepted declaration is more than 30 days old (successor takeover allowance nothing).
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Claire's own declaration writes an accepted intent declaration dated 2026-10-21 and records successor_customer_id = Claire, successor_intent = sell_property, so the successor takeover allowance becomes 14 and the extension 40 instead of 30 (26 raised to the floor).

edges.condition: The Summit case's variant_name reads Death of Last Surviving Borrower, which on such a case is written together with the resolution deadline carried forward by the successor runway days.
edges.policy_source: A first extension on a case whose event was superseded by the borrower's death is not sized until the case's event type reads the death of the last surviving borrower.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The case's event type still reads Property Charge Default and its resolution deadline is the unadjusted 2026-10-24.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The reclassification types the case as a death case and carries the resolution deadline to 2026-11-26, so the aged-listing measurement runs 4 days instead of 37 and the extension becomes 40 instead of 73.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The edges form a chain runway -> successor notices -> successor declaration -> first extension, with the extension also waiting on the runway; every write therefore has exactly one place: the reclassification first (both the notices and the extension wait on the death event type), the notices second (the declaration waits on the successor response deadline they write), the declaration third (the extension waits on the successor's recorded declaration), the extension last. No two writes are unordered, so there is a single topological order and a single terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the reclassification the case keeps variant_name Property Charge Default and resolution_deadline 2026-10-24 in the terminal state; the successor notices would go out on a case still typed as a charge default (state gate), and through the chain the extension computed later changes from 40 to 73.

Without the successor notices the response deadline stays 2026-05-24 (already passed) and the declaration is not taken; computed anyway, the clock would start on that lapsed deadline (resolution deadline more than 30 days after it): evidence_due_days 1 instead of 14, and the terminal state lacks both notices and keeps the old response deadline.

Without Claire's declaration the most recent accepted declaration is Harriet's of 2026-05-11, more than 30 days old, so the successor takeover allowance is 0: 4 + 15 + 7 + 10 - 10 = 26, raised to the 30-day floor, extension_days 30 instead of 40 (extended deadline 2026-12-26 instead of 2027-01-05), and the case keeps Harriet as successor_customer_id.

Without the reclassification the aged-listing measurement runs from 2026-10-24 to 2026-11-30: horizon 37, then 37 + 15 + 7 + 10 + 14 - 10 = 73: extension_days 73 instead of 40, and the case keeps the charge-default event type.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: Claire's lines ask only about the time to finish the sale and the extension request her mother filed; she never mentions reclassifying the case, being sent new notices or a response window, or making a declaration of her own. Her cooperation with the declaration is a passive reaction: only when the agent explains that she must file her own declaration and hands her the tool does she run it with the details the agent gives.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: None of the four tool bodies in task_tools.py checks the case's event type, response deadline, recorded declaration or request status: reclassify_case_to_death_eeacbce3 only updates the case; mail_successor_due_notices_bb6e23d7 creates the two notice entries and sets the response deadline; declare_successor_intent_94ee6efc creates the declaration and records it; grant_first_extension_77f15011 writes the extension, the letter and the status/deadline/request updates. Each returns its receipt whatever state the prerequisites are in; the only Error return is for a case reference that does not exist.
